Do you feel differently about a Voater if their profile is full of porn submissions/comment? Are you more or less likely to respond positively too them?

I doubt I'd bother to look it up.

However, it does remind me that what I would like to see on voat is the possibility of not making your comment history generally viewable. It seems to me that this feature on reddit leads to more ill than good, with people regularly arguing with someone by going into their comment history and picking on something else they said in the past.

I think each comment should stand on its own, there's no need for each user to have a readily-browsable comment history. But since some people would like it and some people wouldn't, it should be a flag.

I like it if I can look up someone's previous comments, but I generally don't look at them. I've got better things to do ^^

Also, porn doesn't bother me. Certain other things might influence my opinion, but I try to see each comment standing on their own.

From Voat's FAQ:

Can I submit links to sites I operate?

Submitting only links to sites you operate (or are associated with), without submitting other, unrelated links, is considered spamming. If you submit niche content (for example gaming videos from your own YouTube channel), you should create your own subverse and submit the content only to that subverse. If majority of the links you submit are to sites you are associated with, your domains may be globally banned from Voat. To be on the safe side, if you submit 10 links to various subverses on Voat, at most 2 of the 10 submitted links may be to the sites you are associated with.

I really think this rule is unintentionally harmful. Many creative professionals (myself included) like to share what we create with the internet, often linking to where we choose to host it. OC that links to sites I'm associated with is all I really have to contribute to this site. If I had to limit those posts to 20% of my content, I would be forced to post 80% of shitty filler and reposts.

Also creating my own subverse would not help me because I do not have a large enough following online and would only be talking to myself. Even if I did have a large enough following, I would barely be contributing to the overall voat community and only contributing to my already existent following.

I'm curious to hear feedback from the community on their stance on this rule.
I think Voat's anti-spam rules are anti-OC and harm the community.
I feel like this rule works on the major subs but you are correct about the small subs. Seems like something the mods should choose to do or not do....we have mods right?
Maybe an addition like "These rules do not apply if you post slowly" would help? With slowly being defined as "3 links/week or less" or something like that.

"This rule may be overridden by the rules set out by a sub".

Leave it up to the moderators, but leave it as a default, in other words.
I think its fine, really not anti-oc.
